module_title: Introduction to Diseases, Pathogens, and Vectors
introduction: A disease is any condition that impairs the normal functioning of the body. They are primarily of two types: Communicable (infectious, spreading from person to person) and Non-communicable (like Cancer or Diabetes). Infectious diseases are caused by microscopic 'Pathogens'.

core_concepts.title: What are Pathogens?
core_concepts.description:
Pathogens are disease-causing microorganisms that invade our bodies. 
There are 4 main types: 
1. Bacteria 
2. Viruses 
3. Fungi 
4. Protozoa

core_concepts.title: What are Vectors?
core_concepts.description:
Some organisms do NOT cause the disease themselves but act as 'Carriers' to transport the pathogen from an infected person to a healthy person. These carriers are called Vectors. 
Examples: Mosquitoes, Houseflies, Rats.

core_concepts.title: How Antibiotics Work
core_concepts.description: Antibiotics (like Penicillin) are chemicals that kill or stop the growth of 'Bacteria'. They generally work by destroying the bacterial 'Cell Wall', causing the bacteria to burst and die. Alexander Fleming discovered the first antibiotic (Penicillin).

important_entities.name: Antibiotics vs. Viruses
important_entities.significance: Examiners love this question: 'Why don't antibiotics cure the Common Cold?' Answer: Because the common cold is caused by a 'Virus'. Viruses do not have a cell wall or their own cellular machinery for the antibiotic to destroy, so antibiotics are completely useless against them.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Remember, ONLY 'Female' mosquitoes bite humans and drink blood (they need the protein from our blood to develop their eggs). 'Male' mosquitoes NEVER bite humans; they survive purely on plant nectar.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Pathogen = The Criminal, Vector = The Getaway Car
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In Malaria, 'Plasmodium' is the criminal (Pathogen) doing the actual damage, and the 'Female Anopheles Mosquito' is just the car (Vector) dropping it into your bloodstream.

exam_strategy_tips: A guaranteed SSC/Railway question: 'Who discovered the first antibiotic, Penicillin?' Answer: Alexander Fleming.
